subject: Chemistry
unit: Unit I — Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
title: Atomic Mass Scales, Isotopic Averages & Dulong-Petit Law
quickSummary: The atomic mass scale is unified to 1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom. For solid heavy metallic elements, the Dulong-Petit Law provides an empirical approach to derive exact atomic mass through approximate atomic mass, equivalent mass, and integer valency.
summary: Master isotopic average calculations and the classic Dulong-Petit analytical method for finding exact atomic mass.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 The Unified Atomic Mass Scale (u / Dalton Da)
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 The Unified Atomic Mass Scale (u / Dalton Da)

summaryBox.title: The Unified Scale Definition
summaryBox.takeaway: 1 u = 1 Da = 1/12 × mass of neutral ¹²C atom = 1/N_A g ≈ 1.66054 × 10⁻²⁴ g = 1.66054 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.

conceptBreakdown.content:
The standard atomic mass unit is defined strictly relative to the Carbon-12 isotope:

$$\mathbf{1\text{ u} = 1\text{ Da} = \frac{1}{12} \times \text{Mass of one neutral }^{12}\text{C atom} = \frac{1}{N_A}\text{ g} \approx 1.66054 \times 10^{-24}\text{ g}}$$

• **Relative Atomic Mass (A_r)**: The dimensionless ratio of the average mass of an element's atom to 1/12th the mass of a ¹²C atom.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Average Atomic Mass Calculations
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Average Atomic Mass Calculations
conceptBreakdown.content:
Naturally occurring elements exist as isotopic mixtures. The Average Atomic Mass (Ā) is the abundance-weighted average:

$$\mathbf{\bar{A} = \sum (f_i \cdot A_i) = \frac{\sum (\%_i \cdot A_i)}{100}}$$

*Example*: Chlorine exists as ³⁵Cl (75.77%, 34.969 u) and ³⁷Cl (24.23%, 36.966 u). Ā = (0.7577 × 35) + (0.2423 × 37) ≈ 35.5 u.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.3 Dulong-Petit Law for Heavy Solid Metals
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.3 Dulong-Petit Law for Heavy Solid Metals
conceptBreakdown.content:
An empirical relationship for determining the approximate atomic mass of solid metallic elements (excluding light non-metals like Be, B, C, Si):

$$\mathbf{\text{Approx. Atomic Mass} \times \text{Specific Heat (cal/g}\cdot^\circ\text{C)} \approx 6.4}$$
$$\mathbf{\text{Approx. Atomic Mass} \times \text{Specific Heat (J/g}\cdot\text{K)} \approx 26.8}$$

**Four-Step Protocol to Find Exact Atomic Mass**:
1. Approx. Atomic Mass = 6.4 / Specific Heat (in cal/g·°C).
2. Determine Equivalent Mass = (Mass of Metal / Mass of Cl) × 35.45 (or from oxide/hydride).
3. Valency = Approx. Atomic Mass / Equivalent Mass (rounded to the nearest integer).
4. **Exact Atomic Mass = Equivalent Mass × Valency**.

quickRevision: Dulong-Petit Law gives ONLY approximate atomic mass.
Exact Atomic Mass = Equivalent Mass × Valency.
